title: Convergence sync prep: Product + Eng + Applied ML (scratch)
body:
Meeting: Product + Eng + Applied ML convergence sync (informal prep)
Owner: Kai Chen (notes)
Proposed time: 2026-04-16 09:30 PT (30–45m) — agenda to be finalised in this doc
Attendees (target): Maya (Product), Eli (Infra/Serving), Sana (Applied ML), Rowan (Console), me (Eng runtime) + optional: Jess (SRE)
Primary goal: agree on an initial cross-team plan to ship the chat prefix caching pilot and the model-routing canary so that Product can present a safe ETA to customer-success by EOW.

Context / why this matters:
- Customer teams are seeing variable P95 latencies on short-chat flows (2–4 turns). Prefix/KV cache could drop per-token compute by avoiding repeated key recomputation.
- Product wants a low-risk dedicated beta (subset of customers + hosted tier) before recommending default enablement in Console.
- Applied ML has concerns about cache correctness for models with stateful recency features and hallucination regression risk.
- Infra/Serving needs clear constraints (SLA, memory budget per instance, eviction policy) before enabling in Dedicated pools.

Top-line agenda:
1) Quick alignment on scope & success metrics (5m)
2) Proposed pilot architecture + invariants (10m)
3) Risk matrix (APPLIED ML concerns + SRE risk) (8m)
4) Rollout plan + canary criteria (10m)
5) Action items & owners (5m)

Proposed success metrics (we should pick 2–3):
- Latency: reduce median token generation latency by >= 15% for chat flows with >1 prompt turn (measured at service ingress, P50/P95)
- Cost: reduce GPU token cost by >= 10% for pilot traffic (tracked by token-level cost breakdown)
- Correctness: no statistically significant increase in hallucination rate on the eval prompt set (applied-ml will define the metric and threshold)

Pilot architecture (sketch):
- Prefix/KV cache layer sits in front of runtime per model-variant. Cached entries keyed by (model-id, quant-level, prefix-hash, customer-id-sample?)
- Cache TTL: short (5–30 minutes) for chat sessions; propose starting at 10m
- Memory guardrails: per-GPU cache budget (configurable) + LRU eviction
- Routing: only route cached-eligible requests to a +cache variant. Non-eligible requests skip caching.
- Canary: start with small % of Hosted API traffic on redwood-7b-q4_0 (or similar low-memory model) for customers opted-in via console flag

Open questions / tensions to surface in the meeting:
- Keying: Should we include customer-scoped keys or make keys global to maximize hits? (Privacy vs hit-rate tradeoff).
- Eval sets: Applied ML needs an eval harness for the pilot. Do we run offline before canary? How many prompts? Who owns?
- Fallback semantics: if cache miss or cache-unavailable, do we fall back to the same model instance or redirect to non-cache variant? (Impacts consistency and latency spikes)
- Metrics instrumentation: need token-level attribution for cached vs non-cached tokens; Rowan/Console should confirm metrics deck availability.
- Billing/Costing: If cached responses reduce GPU time, how do we reflect that to customer invoices (deduct vs internal)? Finance/product conversation needed.

Risks & mitigations (quick bullets):
- Regressions in output quality: mitigation = baseline A/B with applied-ml eval + holdback group, short canary window, rollback flag in Console.
- Memory pressure causing OOMs: mitigation = conservative per-GPU budgets + circuit-breaker that disables cache when memory > threshold.
- Cache poisoning (malicious repeated prefixes): mitigation = rate-limit keys per customer and TTLs + validation checks.
- Complexity for Dedicated customers: mitigation = opt-in per-dedicated-pool config; default off.

Rollout proposal (phased):
- Phase 0 (internal): small internal traffic run, engineer-in-loop, 1–2 days. Owner: Eli.
- Phase 1 (hosted opt-in beta): 1% Hosted API traffic from opted-in customers via Console flag, 1 week. Owner: Maya/Product.
- Phase 2 (wider canary): 10% hosted traffic + a couple dedicated pools flagged for beta customers, 2–3 weeks. Owner: Rowan/Infra.
- Phase 3 (gradual default enable): enable-by-default for low-memory model variants after 4 weeks of positive signals. Owner: Product.

Canary criteria (proposed pass/fail):
- Latency: no >20% increase in P95 vs baseline; median improves or unchanged.
- Quality: hallucination metric delta <= predefined threshold from Applied ML.
- Stability: no OOM events attributable to caching, error rate stable (<0.1% delta).

Concrete action items (first pass):
- Applied ML (Sana): define hallucination/regression eval set + automated run for pilot by 2026-04-20.
- Infra/Serving (Eli): prototype per-GPU cache budget and circuit-breaker; demo internal run by 2026-04-22.
- Product (Maya): draft customer opt-in flow for Console + telemetry flags by 2026-04-21.
- Console (Rowan): add telemetry tag for cached-vs-noncached tokens and dashboard stub by 2026-04-25.
- Me (Kai): write short runbook for rollback + list of required feature flags and config knobs (due 2026-04-20).

Notes-to-self / conversation starters for the meeting:
- Start the meeting with the single-sentence framing: "We want to validate that prefix caching yields predictable latency/cost wins without hurting quality — here's a minimal, reversible path to test it."
- Push for a single owner per deliverable — avoids triage delays.
- Ask Applied ML to propose a quick pre-canary offline test that doesn't require infra changes (run models locally on sample prompts).
- Keep the first canary small and reversible; prefer to iterate on metrics before broad rollout.

Related tickets/PRs to have handy in meeting:
- INF-1324 (kv-cache prototype)
- PR: serving-runtime#987 (cache eviction + budget implementation)
- Confluence: kv-cache-proposal (design doc)

If we run out of time, prioritise: 1) success metrics, 2) canary pass/fail criteria, 3) first owners & short deadlines.

TBD (things to follow up after meeting):
- Finance alignment on cost attribution model for caching wins
- Security review for any customer-keying or shared-cache decisions
- Dedicated pool UX for enabling cache (console + infra docs)

End notes: keep this as a living scratch doc — will copy into a Confluence summary after we have owners and dates.
